notes: Rule list confirmed against evals/README.md: 15 rows name code-review, the same 15 as the 2026-10-21 grade files.

Method and mapping are the 2026-10-21 baseline's: 20 planted problems (the 18 table rows, with lines 15-17 split into rebinding and magic 120, and line 45 into spawn and closure copy); the 10-40 nesting belongs to both 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...'; lines 32 and 36,39 to 'Match every expected shape'; the comments and both magic numbers to 'Comments explain why...'; the line 8 raise outside the try and the 10-40 try/rescue to 'Return {:ok, value}...'; lines 12 and 51 to the pipeline rule; the line 21 dead is_binary maps to no rule and is tracked in reported/missed only. A problem counts as reported only if a finding names it or the finding's stated fix addresses it; a silent fix in the improved code, or a mention only under a 'Behavior changes' or 'Changes callers will notice' section, does not count. A rule is violated if a planted problem belonging to it went unreported or the improved code still contains it, else clean.

Baseline standards kept: a one-line `if ..., do:` in a `with` body is not counted as nesting; a `_ ->` inside `case Integer.parse(...)` is not counted; a `fix: min(age, 120)` does not report the magic 120; an assumed `User` changeset function counts as a changeset even when the age floor is still checked by hand.

Rules changed since 93873be (git diff 93873be -- idiomatic-elixir/): 'Validate input with changesets' now adds 'A `%User{}` built from the params and passed to `Repo.insert/1` is the pattern to replace: Ecto inserts the struct as given, so nothing is validated and a constraint violation raises.' That sentence decides the violated verdicts for haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2, which still insert a `%User{}` built from the params. For opus-1 the unchanged sentence 'Cast and validate external input with `Ecto.Changeset` (...) instead of checking fields by hand' decides it: its `change/1` casts and validates nothing. Sonnet-1's `Repo.insert(User.import_changeset(%User{}, attrs))` matches the new example and stays clean. 'Match every expected shape' changed only its example (`_data` to `_payload`) and is graded to the old standard. No other graded rule changed.

Changed rules outside the list, used only for other_violations: the Naming bullet now says 'A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job', which decides the haiku-1 and sonnet-1 entries; the 'Chain fallible steps with `with`' rule gained the one-step-`with` sentences, which no run breaks (haiku-2's entry rests on the unchanged 'let `with` pass the error through unchanged'). Missing `Keyword.validate!/2` on `opts` is not listed for any run, as the previous sweep did not list it.

Judgment calls on 'reported': opus-1's line 32 counts through finding 4, which names 'the `_ -> {:error, :insert_failed}` branch on line 32' and whose fix makes duplicates return `{:error, changeset}`; opus-1's lines 36,39 do not count, since finding 4 is about exceptions relabelled as `:invalid` and the specific per-field errors appear only under 'Changes callers will notice' (review.md line 30), the treatment the previous sweep gave its opus-1 line 32 and its skill haiku-2 lines 36,39. Sonnet-2's lines 36,39 count through finding 3's fix ('return tagged errors (`:invalid_role`, `:invalid_email`, `:invalid_age`, `:underage`)'); haiku-1 finding 5 and haiku-2 finding 4 only say the rescue turns exceptions into `:invalid` and do not count. Sonnet-1's line 21 `&&` counts through finding 9's bullet '`&&`/`!` on booleans: prefer `and`/`not` where values are strictly boolean.' (review.md line 25): line 21 holds the only `&&` with strictly boolean operands, the qualifier excludes line 26, and the bullet quotes no line. Haiku-2's line 45 spawn does not count: finding 2 says the `spawn` crash goes unreported and swaps in `Task.start/1` 'so crashes are logged', never naming supervision. Haiku-1's comments row counts through finding 8 although it says the module comment 'can stay'. Sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 count the line 8 raise through 'It also raises on a missing `"role"` key' / '...and that happens outside the `try`', as the previous skill grade did.

Must-not-report lines: no run reports line 11, 19 or 26 as a problem. Opus-1 finding 9's line 19 point is blank CSV cells, not the access or `||`, as in the previous sweep. Sonnet-2 finding 9 calls `opts[:notify] && !opts[:silent]` hard to read and names the override, but never says `&&`/`!` are wrong, so it is not counted as a false positive.
findings_name_rule_and_quote is 'partly' for every run: findings quote code fragments (opus-1 also gives input line numbers), but no finding names a rule.
Evidence line numbers are review.md line numbers; 'input line' means code-review-input.ex.
